## Recommendation: Hold

**Why the ledger alone can't answer this**: both hypotheses are UNRESOLVED because T2 — the one test that would tell you whether the 57ms gap is a real regression (H1) or an exporter artifact (H2) — never ran (raw logs pending restore). Everything below is a substitute for that missing test, not a replacement for running it if you still can.

**What the existing evidence is worth**: T3's reference class (20 past rollouts, quota-sampled 10/10 by outcome) can't tell you a base rate, but it *can* tell you a likelihood ratio — that's exactly what quota/case-control sampling preserves even though it distorts prevalence. In past rollouts, a >40ms gap showed up in 9/10 real regressions vs. 2/10 non-regressions: **LR = 4.5** in favor of "real" whenever the gap is observed (as it was here, at 57ms).

Updating your stated prior (1/50 to 1/5) by that LR:

| Your prior | Posterior P(real regression) |
|---|---|
| 1/50 (0.02) | 8.4% |
| 1/5 (0.20) | 52.9% |
| geometric-mean prior (0.063) | 23.3% |

**Where the cost disagreement matters**: ship if the posterior is below `1/(1+k)`, where k is the miss-cost/hold-cost ratio. That threshold works out to:

| Prior | Cost ratio k needed to justify holding |
|---|---|
| 0.02 | k > 10.9 |
| 0.10 | k > 2.0 |
| 0.20 | k > 0.9 (always, given your range) |

Your team's k range (2–20) sits above these thresholds for almost the whole prior range — only the corner where the prior is near 1/50 *and* the cost ratio is near 2 favors shipping. Checked against the full stated ranges as a grid, **~73% of the plausible prior × cost-ratio combinations favor holding**, and both natural "middle of the range" estimates (geometric-mean prior with geometric-mean cost ratio → posterior 23% vs. a 14% ship threshold) land on hold too.

**Bottom line**: the decision isn't airtight — genuine edge cases in your stated ranges would justify shipping — but holding is the better bet under most of the uncertainty you described, not a coin flip. If there's any way to expedite the S3 log restore before Friday, that's worth more than this whole calculation: it's the one test that turns this from a probabilistic call into a settled one.
